text:
Coatesville Medicaid spending on Surgery services totals $7,083 in 2024
In 2024, Medicaid providers in Coatesville submitted $7,083 in claims for the Surgery service category, data from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database show. This figure reflects a 3.9% rise from 2023, when claims under the same category totaled $6,819.
Medicaid is a state-administered, publicly funded health insurance program supported by both federal and state governments. It assists low-income residents, children, seniors, and people with disabilities, making it a significant component of the nation’s health care system.
As Medicaid spending is taxpayer-funded, fluctuations in local billing help show how communities allocate public health care resources.
The "Surgery" category encompasses Medicaid services grouped by the nature of care, classified through standard HCPCS and CPT codes. For the purposes of this report, each billing code was assigned to one primary category based on code prefixes and numerical groupings, which keeps services grouped accurately, prevents duplication, and maintains tracking consistency.
Other Medicaid service types also saw spending increases, but Surgery ranked eighth in Coatesville based on total Medicaid payments for 2024.
Statewide in Pennsylvania, Surgery stood at 16th by payment total among Medicaid categories in 2024.
Looking at the five years up to 2024, Medicaid payments related to Surgery in Coatesville rose by $6,815, equaling 2547%. This growth included periods of rapid year-over-year increases, especially in 2021 and 2023.
Within the city, payments for Surgery services were concentrated in specific ZIP codes. In 2024, ZIP code 19320 recorded $7,082 in Medicaid payments for Surgery, accounting for 100% of the city’s total in this service category that year.
Only a small number of billing codes made up the bulk of Surgery-related Medicaid payments in Coatesville.
Comparing year-over-year changes, Surgery category Medicaid payments in Coatesville increased by 3.9% from 2023 to 2024, versus a 5.2% rise for all Medicaid claim categories in the city during that period.
According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, joint federal and state Medicaid spending reached nearly $871.7 billion in fiscal year 2023, about 18% of national health expenditures—an increase from $613.5 billion pre-pandemic, in 2019.
Much of this approximately 40% increase came from expanded Medicaid enrollment and higher utilization throughout and following the COVID-19 pandemic.
Recent federal budget measures introduced significant proposals to reduce federal Medicaid funding and alter program structure. For example, the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” signed into law in 2025, is expected to trim over $1 trillion in federal Medicaid spending during the next decade and bring in work requirements and more cost-sharing for some recipients. These changes may increase the share of expenses managed by states and slow the pace of federal Medicaid growth as the program continues to cover millions of Americans.
